label: def:q-momentum
title: $q$-Momentum from the braid writhe
html:
Definition. q-Momentum from the braid writhe

The q-momentum of a particle is the braid writhe of its canonical representative — the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form at the minimal level of the brane tower — weighted by the Hecke deformation parameter.

Definition. Let \beta \in B_n be the canonical braid representative of a particle knot K = \hat{\beta} (braid closure), with generators \sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k} where \epsilon_j = \pm 1. The q-momentum is:

  p_q(\beta) =  \sum_{j=1}^{k} [\epsilon_j]_q
  =  \sum_{j=1}^{k} \frac{q^{\epsilon_j} - q^{-\epsilon_j}}{q - q^{-1}}
  =  \sum_{j=1}^{k} \epsilon_j = w(\beta)

where [\epsilon]_q = (q^{\epsilon} - q^{-\epsilon})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer, defined for q \neq \pm 1 (so that q - q^{-1} \neq 0). On that domain, [+1]_q = 1 and [-1]_q = -1 exactly. Each crossing contributes precisely its sign, and the q-momentum coincides with the classical writhe w(\beta) for all such q — not only in the limit q \to 1 (where the removable 0/0 singularity of [\pm 1]_q takes the same values \pm 1). The q-deformation operates trivially at single crossings; it would distinguish multi-strand contributions |\epsilon| \geq 2, but these do not occur in a braid word.

Equivalently, the q-momentum is the trace of the braid in the fundamental representation of H_n(R, q):

  p_q(\beta) =  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{fund}}(\rho(\beta))

where \rho: B_n \to H_n(R, q) is the Hecke representation.

Why the representative must be canonical. The writhe is not a link invariant. Conjugation \beta \mapsto \gamma\beta\gamma^{-1} — the horizontal direction of the brane tower — preserves it, but stabilisation \beta \in B_n \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} \in B_{n+1} presents the same link and shifts it by \pm 1. Both facts are proved sorry-free in QOU/StandardModel/WritheMarkovInvariance.lean (writhe_conj, writhe_stabilize). So p_q is a function of the braid word, and becomes a function of the particle only after the level is pinned; the framework pins it at the minimal level, where the surviving moves are horizontal. The single datum of the pair (w, n) that survives the vertical move unaided is the parity (w - n) \bmod 2, which is the component parity of the closure (QOU/StandardModel/WritheLevelParity.lean) and carries one bit — far too little to serve as p_q.
